name: Doodh Patti Chai
description: Rich Pakistani doodh patti made by simmering black tea with milk, sugar and optional cardamom for a strong, comforting cup.
ingredients: 2 to 3 tsp sugar, or to taste
2 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed, optional
method: Add the milk to a saucepan with the optional water and cardamom, and heat gently while watching closely so it does not boil over.
Add the black tea leaves and sugar once the liquid is hot, then stir to dissolve the sugar.
Bring the chai to a controlled boil, lower the heat and simmer briefly until the colour deepens and the tea strength suits you.
Avoid extending the boil excessively to force a darker colour, as prolonged brewing can make the tea harsh.
Strain directly into cups and serve hot. Adjust tea quantity or simmering time on the next batch if you prefer a stronger or lighter doodh patti.
image_alt: Pakistani doodh patti chai made with milk, black tea and optional green cardamom
image_caption: Rich doodh patti simmered with black tea, milk and optional cardamom until balanced and strong.
technique: Doodh patti is milk-forward, so watch both tea extraction and milk heat. A darker cup is not automatically better; stop when the tea is strong enough before the leaves make the milk tea drying or harsh.
doneness_cues: The milk should be hot and steaming without a scorched smell.
Tea colour should deepen gradually after the leaves are added.
The finished cup should taste rounded and milky with clear black-tea flavour rather than bitterness.
mistakes: Boiling the tea for a long time simply to force a dark colour.
Leaving milk unattended where it can overflow or catch.
Using cardamom so heavily that it becomes masala chai rather than simple doodh patti.
substitutions: The optional 1/4 cup water gives the tea leaves an easier extraction stage and can be omitted for a richer milk-only style.
Cardamom can be omitted for a plain doodh patti.
Adjust sugar after the tea reaches its final strength.
storage: Best served freshly strained. If refrigerated, cool promptly and keep covered; milk tea loses aroma during long storage.
reheating: Warm gently until steaming and avoid repeated boiling, which over-extracts any remaining tea particles and flattens the milk flavour.
serving: Strain into two cups and serve hot, ideally soon after brewing.
tips: Use a saucepan with enough headroom because milk rises quickly.
Judge tea strength by taste, not colour alone.
For a stronger next batch, change leaf quantity slightly rather than greatly extending the boil.

faqs.question: Why is my doodh patti bitter?
faqs.answer: The tea leaves were likely too strong for the milk or boiled too long. Shorten extraction first.

faqs.question: Does doodh patti need water?
faqs.answer: No. Some versions use only milk; a small amount of water is an optional way to help tea extraction and lighten the cup.

faqs.question: Why is my doodh patti pale?
faqs.answer: The tea quantity may be light or the leaves may need a little more controlled extraction. Increase leaf quantity slightly before resorting to a very long boil.
